oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: SLA breach detected for tenant 'volta-foods' (vol-982). p99 latency 2200ms (> 1500ms SLA), error rate 5% over 5m. Pages sent to #eng-oncall.

maria g.: on it, looking at dashboards now. pls hold pages if we can triage quickly.

kevin l.: I see a concentrated spike from a single origin IP pool hitting /generate concurrently. qps triple baseline. p50 ok, p95 elevated, p99 blown out.

kevin l.: Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/tenant-ops?view=vol-982

derek (eng-sre): can we confirm whether this tenant is on Dedicated or Hosted? if Dedicated, might be tenant-level burst shaping config.

maria g.: Volta is hosted. No dedicated capacity. Looks like a sudden regen job — many short sessions with long context. KV cache miss rate jumped.

sara: KV cache miss -> more compute per request, explains p99. For immediate relief: suggest temporary alert suppression for vol-982 to reduce noisy pages, AND enable fallback route to a cheaper, smaller model variant for this tenant for 10m.

maria g.: Agreed. Starting suppression: opsbot can we create a suppression rule for alert id "svc:latency:vol-982" for 20m? mark as mitigation-only.

opsbot: Suppression created: id=SUPP-8712, scope=tenant:vol-982, duration=20m, created_by=maria g. :white_check_mark:

kevin l.: I'll also add a temporary routing rule: route vol-982 -> model:redwood-small-2025 fallback with rate-limit 50r/s. Should reduce p99 immediately.

maria g.: Command I used to mute alert via alertmanager API:

```
# mute with Alertmanager
curl -XPOST "https://alertmanager.redwood.com/api/v2/silences" -d '{\n  "matchers": [{"name":"tenant","value":"vol-982","isRegex":false}],\n  "startsAt": "2026-08-15T15:40:30Z",\n  "endsAt": "2026-08-15T16:00:30Z",\n  "createdBy": "maria g.",\n  "comment": "temporary noise suppression while we route to fallback model"\n}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
```

kevin l.: routed and rate-limited. Verified model fallback serving from edge with lower mem footprint. p99 dropped to ~900ms on the route.

maria g.: Nice. Error rate also dropping. Re-opening pages if we see regression. For follow-up: we should tune the tenant-specific heartbeat check — current check is p999 over 5m which is too sensitive for hosted tenants with bursty workloads.

derek (eng-sre): +1. Proposal: change tenant SLA check from p999->p99 for alerts (keep p999 for auto-escalation to internal reliability metric but not paging) and add a 15m aggregation window plus a suppression threshold multiplier for tenants flagged as "noisy".

sara: Concrete suggestion:
- Alert type: SLA_P99_LATENCY
- Severity: page -> only if p99 > 2x SLA for 10m
- For tenant-specific check add a noise-suppression label and default suppression window 15m
- Create per-tenant dashboard with p50/p95/p99 and cache-miss rate panels

maria g.: I'll open a quick ticket and create a minimal dashboard template for per-tenant ops. Ticket: https://rwd.atlassian.com/browse/OPS-4127

natalie: i'm taking 1st-line at 15:30 UTC. handing off: vol-982 is suppressed (SUPP-8712) and routed to redwood-small until 16:00 UTC, p99 currently ~920ms. docs in ticket OPS-4127.

maria g.: thanks natalie. playbook items for handoff:
- check suppression id SUPP-8712 status
- watch Grafana panel for vol-982 for CPU, cache-miss, and tail latency
- if p99 climbs >1500ms again, escalate to eng-runtime and remove suppression (we'll let pages through)

natalie: copied. also, suggest we add a short-term dashboard alarm to catch sudden cache-miss rate jumps (alert type: cache-miss-rate > 4x baseline over 3m) so we can reactive route earlier.

derek (eng-sre): post-incident owner here. Action items:
- Update tenant alerting rules: p999 -> p99 for paging; add "noisy tenant" suppression label and default 15m suppress window (owner: derek)
- Template: per-tenant Grafana dashboard (owner: maria)
- Add playbook section about fallback routing and rate-limits (owner: sara)
- Add tests in canary to simulate cache-miss noise so alert adjustments don't regress (owner: kevin)

maria g.: i'll start the dashboard template PR now.

opsbot: NOTE: suppression SUPP-8712 will expire at 2026-08-15T16:00:30Z unless extended or removed.

kevin l.: one more follow-up: consider instrumenting origin IP cardinality per tenant — high cardinality correlates with regen-bots. cheap metric to compute and useful for automated mitigation.

maria g.: added to OPS-4127.

sara: postmortem to include customer impact assessment: how many requests failed, token cost delta, whether SLA credit needed. Let's schedule async follow-up tomorrow.

natalie: confirmed, I'll take the postmortem write-up.

maria g.: thanks team, closing live thread. will update OPS-4127 with timeline and config diffs. :white_check_mark:
